thread:
maya: FYI customer reported 401s from the browser when calling the Node/TS SDK from a Vercel Edge function. Works in Postman. They say intermittent 401s and CORS console errors.
samir: Can you paste the browser console error and the SDK version they're using?
maya: Console: "Access to fetch at 'https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate' from origin 'https://app.customer.com' has been blocked by CORS request" then a 401 in our logs. SDK version: @redwood/inference-js@0.12.3. Runtime: Vercel Edge (edge middleware). Customer code (minimal):

```js
// edge function
import Redwood from '@redwood/inference-js'
const client = new Redwood({ apiKey: process.env.RW_KEY })

export default async (req) => {
  const res = await client.generate({ model: 'gpt-xyz', prompt: 'hi' })
  return new Response(await res.text(), { status: 200 })
}
```

maya: They said they tried sending the Authorization header manually with fetch from the browser and saw preflight failures. In Postman (no preflight) it works.
olivia: Sounds like a CORS preflight + header allow issue. If the request from browser triggers OPTIONS and the API doesn't include Authorization in Access-Control-Allow-Headers the browser will block before the request hits us. But you said logs show 401, so some requests are reaching our API and being rejected.
samir: Two possibilities: (1) the SDK or edge adapter is changing header casing/ordering and a downstream CDN or auth middleware expects canonical ordering/signature, or (2) Vercel Edge is stripping or rewriting headers for forwarded requests. Any chance the customer is using a custom signing middleware on their side?
maya: Customer says no signing, just standard Authorization: `Bearer <key>`. We pulled request traces: one trace shows incoming request with header `authorization: Bearer abc...` and our auth check returned 401 because header value got truncated to `Bearer` (no token). Other traces are fine.
olivia: That truncation rings a bell — we had a bug in 0.12.x where Headers serialization in the edge fetch shim accidentally called `toString()` on the Headers iterator, which in some runtimes produced comma-separated values that caused middleware downstream to parse incorrectly. Fixed in 0.13.1.
maya: Customer is on 0.12.3. They can't easily move key to server backend; they're trying to keep calls in the edge function because they need low latency. What's the quick mitigation?
support-bot: Suggestion: (a) upgrade the SDK to >=0.13.1; (b) as a workaround, set the Authorization header explicitly using a plain object on the fetch override (if using custom fetch) or use a serverless function (not edge) that proxies and injects the key. Example override:

```js
// override fetch inside edge adapter
const res = await fetch('https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate', {
  method: 'POST',
  headers: { 'authorization': `Bearer ${process.env.RW_KEY}`, 'content-type': 'application/json' },
  body: JSON.stringify({ model: 'gpt-xyz', prompt: 'hi' })
})
```

olivia: Also check that the API responds to OPTIONS with `Access-Control-Allow-Headers: Authorization, Content-Type` and `Access-Control-Allow-Origin: https://app.customer.com` (or `*` for testing). Browser preflight will fail otherwise.
samir: If you need a repro, ask the customer to run a curl that simulates the browser preflight + actual request. Example:

```bash
curl -i -X OPTIONS 'https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate' \
  -H 'Origin: https://app.customer.com' \
  -H 'Access-Control-Request-Method: POST' \
  -H 'Access-Control-Request-Headers: Authorization,Content-Type'
```

If that returns 200 with the right headers, preflight is okay. Then test the POST with the header present.

maya: I asked them to try upgrading to 0.13.1 and to paste the preflight output. They pushed a quick branch: https://github.com/customer/repros/edge-auth-repro

(Logs they pasted) — pre-upgrade OPTIONS reply was missing Authorization in ACAH. After we updated a proxy rule (temporary) the preflight succeeded but we still saw one trace where the Authorization value arrived truncated.
olivia: That truncated token is the SDK serialization bug. Customer will try upgrade. If they can't, tell them to use fetch override as a stopgap.
samir: I'll create a bug: ENG-RUNTIME-568 — header serialization in edge adapters for 0.12.x. Eng-runtime, can you triage and backport a patch to the 0.12 branch? Tagging you here.
eng-runtime: Got it. We'll reproduce using the repro repo, verify behavior on Vercel Edge and Cloudflare Pages, and prepare a patch. If it's urgent, we can cut a 0.12.4 with the fix.
maya: I'll relay back: recommend upgrade, or proxy in middle-tier, or explicit fetch override. Customer opted to upgrade and test. Will follow up with results. :thumbsup:
samir: Thanks — if the upgrade doesn't resolve it, ask them to attach a HAR and the exact SDK call. That'll help us pinpoint any runtime-specific quirks.
maya: Noted. Closing loop once they confirm.
